why: Iso-raise to 4bb + 1bb per limper (6bb here)
Limpers have weak ranges and call too much
Build the pot while you hold the best hand
breakdowns.caption: Aces behind limpers? Make them pay. Raise 4bb + 1 per limper.

breakdowns.hook: Why you should FOLD pocket 2s here
breakdowns.setup: Effective stack 30bb  |  You: Cutoff  |  UTG opens 3bb
why: You flop a set only ~12% of the time
Set-mining needs ~15-20x the call behind
At 30bb you can't win enough when you hit
breakdowns.caption: Set-mining only works when stacks are deep. At 30bb, small pairs are a fold here.

breakdowns.hook: Most players fold AQ here. Big mistake.
why: AQ is way ahead of a button 3-bet range
Too strong to fold, too weak to 4-bet for value
Calling keeps all of his bluffs in the pot
breakdowns.caption: AQ vs a button 3-bet: don't fold it, don't blow it up. Call and play the flop.

breakdowns.setup: 100bb cash  |  You raised preflop  |  Big blind calls
breakdowns.action: Checked to you on a dry flop.
why: K-7-2 rainbow hits YOUR range way more
A small bet wins the pot cheaply a lot
Bet small with almost your whole range here
breakdowns.caption: Dry king-high flop as the raiser? Small c-bet, nearly every hand.

breakdowns.setup: 100bb cash  |  You bet the flop  |  Villain check-raises big
why: This board smashes sets, two pair and straights
Re-raising only gets called by hands that beat you
Call, see the turn, and keep the pot under control
breakdowns.caption: Overpair on a wet board facing a check-raise? Don't go broke. Call and re-evaluate.

breakdowns.hook: Should you chase this flush draw?
breakdowns.setup: 100bb cash  |  Villain bets half pot on the flop
breakdowns.action: You have 9 outs to the nut flush.
why: Half-pot bet = you need 25% equity
You hit ~20% on the turn, ~35% by the river
Nut flush means you get paid when you hit
breakdowns.caption: Nut flush draw vs a half-pot bet is a clear call. Here's the math.

breakdowns.hook: The Rule of 2 and 4 (learn this today)
breakdowns.setup: You flop an open-ended straight draw
breakdowns.action: Any 9 or 4 makes your straight. 8 outs.
why: On the flop: outs x 4 = chance by the river
On the turn: outs x 2 = chance on the river
8 outs = ~32% on the flop, ~16% on the turn
breakdowns.caption: The fastest way to know your odds at the table. Outs x 4 on the flop, x 2 on the turn.

breakdowns.hook: Stop flatting from the small blind
breakdowns.setup: 100bb cash  |  Button opens 2.5bb  |  You: Small blind
why: Calling lets the big blind squeeze you
You're out of position the whole hand
KJ is ahead of a wide button range, so raise
breakdowns.caption: From the small blind vs a button open, 3-bet or fold. Flatting is a leak.

breakdowns.setup: 100bb cash  |  Villain checked turn and river
breakdowns.action: Your straight draw missed. No showdown value.
why: Two checks shows weakness
Your hand can't win at showdown, so bluff it
Bet big enough to fold out pairs
breakdowns.caption: Missed draw, villain checks twice, zero showdown value? That's your bluff.

breakdowns.hook: Top pair is NOT always good
breakdowns.setup: Low-stakes cash  |  Villain bets flop, turn, and river
breakdowns.action: Big river bet. Call with top pair?
why: Three big bets at low stakes = rarely a bluff
Weak kicker loses to every better king
Q9 and many two pairs crush you too
breakdowns.caption: Top pair weak kicker vs three big bets at low stakes? Save your chips.

breakdowns.hook: Free money most players leave on the table
breakdowns.setup: 100bb cash  |  Checked to you on the river
breakdowns.action: Top pair, top kicker. Check it back?
why: Worse queens and 8s will call a small bet
Checking back wins nothing extra
Bet ~1/2 pot: thin value adds up
breakdowns.caption: Top pair top kicker checked to you on the river? Bet. Worse hands call.

breakdowns.hook: Open MORE hands on the button
breakdowns.setup: 100bb cash  |  Folded to you on the button
why: Only the blinds are left to act
You'll have position the whole hand
Good players open ~45% of hands from here
breakdowns.caption: Folded to you on the button? Raise way more hands than you think.

breakdowns.action: You flopped a set on a scary board.
why: Straights and flushes can come on almost any card
Draws will pay you right now
Charge them before the board gets worse
breakdowns.caption: Set on a wet board? Bet now. Slow-playing here lets draws catch up for free.

breakdowns.setup: Tournament  |  10bb stack  |  Folded to you on the button
why: At 10bb, raise-folding wastes your stack
Shoving wins the blinds without a fight
Any ace is strong when only the blinds can call
breakdowns.caption: Short stack on the button with an ace? It's a shove.

quizzes.q: Folded to you under the gun. What do you do?
quizzes.explain: 7-2 offsuit is the worst hand in poker. Easy fold.
quizzes.caption: The easiest question in poker... right?

quizzes.q: UTG opens. You're on the button. Play?
quizzes.explain: Queens are a value 3-bet. Build the pot and thin the field.
quizzes.caption: Pocket queens on the button facing an open. What's your play?

quizzes.q: Villain checks to you. Best move?
quizzes.explain: Top pair top kicker on a dry board: bet small to get value from worse aces.
quizzes.caption: Top pair top kicker on a dry board. Check, bet, or shove?

quizzes.q: Villain bets POT on the river. What equity do you need to call?
quizzes.caption: Pot odds quiz. Most people get this wrong.

quizzes.q: Villain bets HALF pot. What equity do you need to call?
quizzes.caption: Half-pot bet. How often do you need to win to call?

quizzes.q: How many outs does an open-ended straight draw have?
quizzes.explain: Any 10 or any 5 makes your straight: 4 + 4 = 8 outs.
quizzes.caption: Count your outs. Comment before the reveal.

quizzes.q: How many outs does a flush draw have?
quizzes.explain: 13 hearts total, 4 are showing, so 9 are left.
quizzes.caption: Flush draw outs. Quick math check.

quizzes.q: 9 outs on the flop. Chance to hit by the river?
quizzes.explain: Rule of 4: 9 outs x 4 = ~36% with two cards to come.
quizzes.caption: Rule of 4 quiz. Can you do it in your head?

quizzes.q: Which seat is the most profitable in poker?
quizzes.explain: The button acts last after the flop, every street.
quizzes.caption: Where do the pros make most of their money?

quizzes.q: Aces vs Kings all in preflop. How often do Aces win?
quizzes.explain: Aces win about 81% of the time. Kings still win ~1 in 5.
quizzes.caption: Aces vs kings. How big of a favorite are you really?

quizzes.q: Button min-raises. You're in the big blind. Play?
quizzes.explain: You're getting a great price. Suited connectors defend easily vs a min-raise.
quizzes.caption: 98 suited in the big blind vs a min-raise. Fold or defend?

quizzes.q: Pocket 2s vs Ace-King all in preflop. Who's ahead?
quizzes.explain: It's a coin flip: the pair wins about 52%, AK about 48%.
quizzes.caption: The classic coin flip. Do you know who's ahead?

quizzes.q: Flush draw + gutshot on the flop. Your equity vs top pair?
quizzes.explain: 12 outs on the flop (9 hearts + 3 more tens) = ~45%. Close to a flip!
quizzes.caption: Big draw vs top pair. Who's really ahead?

quizzes.q: How many combinations of Ace-King exist?
quizzes.explain: 4 aces x 4 kings = 16 combos (4 suited, 12 offsuit).
quizzes.caption: Combo counting quiz. This one separates regs from fish.
